rejections.brief: 1600 x 1800; lateral ankle: tibia and fibula cut above the ankle, talus, calcaneus, three lateral ligaments; bones and ligaments only, no skin, toes or foot outline (pending root approval)
rejections.prompt: Use case scientific-educational. Anatomically accurate REGIONAL LATERAL ANKLE plate, house watercolour matching a refined ivory-bone and pale-blue-cartilage knee cutaway with pale fibrous ligament bands. Show ONLY distal tibia and fibula cut cleanly above ankle, talus and calcaneus, and the three lateral ankle ligaments. Anterior/talar neck points RIGHT, posterior heel points LEFT. Slight oblique lateral dissection view exposes the posterior band without changing normal bone positions. The slender distal FIBULA and its lateral malleolus are on the outer side. All THREE named ligament bands attach proximally to DISTAL FIBULA, never the tibia: (1) anterior talofibular ligament: from anterior edge of lateral malleolus forward/right to the lateral talar neck, approximately horizontal; (2) calcaneofibular ligament: from the distal fibular tip diagonally down and backward/left to the lateral surface of CALCANEUS; (3) posterior talofibular ligament: a shorter thicker deep band from the posterior fibular malleolar fossa backward/left to the POSTEROLATERAL TALAR PROCESS, almost horizontal. Both talofibular bands end on TALUS, only calcaneofibular ends on calcaneus. Make their three courses distinct and anatomically correct. No extra ligament substituted for one of these. Fine dark ink edges, watercolour pigment texture, lightly porous clean cut bone ends. 1600 by1800 portrait canvas with genuine transparent alpha around the isolated bones and bands. No skin, toes, whole foot outline, muscles, blood, people, hands, faces, text, labels, numbers, arrows or scale.
rejections.referenceUse: Anatomical facts only; no source images used or adapted.
rejections.reason: Posterior band does not show a distinct attachment to posterior talus and appears to reach calcaneus. Anatomical insertion cannot be accepted.

Add only three clean anatomical muscle forms in the same refined watercolour style: muted rose biceps on the FRONT of upper arm, deeper rose triceps on the BACK of upper arm, and shoulder deltoid over the humeral head. Keep existing ivory bones visible beside or subtly through these muscles. The scapula, clavicle and distal forearm must remain unchanged. Essential attachments: biceps distal tendon ends on the RADIAL TUBEROSITY immediately below the round radius head at the ELBOW, only the very proximal forearm, never halfway down the forearm. On this image the radius is the LEFT forearm bone with a round disc head. Triceps tendon ends on the OLECRANON at the BACK of the elbow, the proximal hook of the RIGHT forearm ulna, not the radius. Deltoid attaches to mid-lateral humerus. Show clean pale tendons at these correct insertions, no blood. No forearm muscle added. No people, skin, hand bones, hands, face, labels, text, arrows or other structures. Genuine alpha transparency outside the combined anatomical structures. Keep exact1001x1572 canvas and exact bone registration.
